A growing list of readings, tools, and examples we draw on throughout the course.
Each week's class page links to its assigned readings.

## Examples to learn from

- Pingfan Hu, [*"Agentic Skills"*](https://pingfanhu.com/blog/2026-06-24-agentic-skills/): how he writes skills for images, slides, and HTML, including generating images with Gemini and finishing them with code so they come out the same every time.
- Pingfan Hu, [*"Agentic Engineering"* Part 1](https://pingfanhu.com/blog/2026-03-26-agentic-engineering-1/), [Part 2](https://pingfanhu.com/blog/2026-04-06-agentic-engineering-2/), and [Part 3](https://pingfanhu.com/blog/2026-04-09-agentic-engineering-3/), plus [*"Agentic Workflows"*](https://pingfanhu.com/blog/2026-05-15-agentic-workflows/).
- Pingfan Hu, [*"How to Make a Personal Website"*](https://pingfanhu.com/blog/2023-12-09-personal-website/) (with Quarto).

## How LLMs work

- 3Blue1Brown, [*Neural networks*](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aircAruvnKk&list=PLZHQObOWTQDNU6R1_67000Dx_ZCJB-3pi) video series.
- [Transformer Explainer](https://poloclub.github.io/transformer-explainer/) and the [tokenizer playground](https://tiktokenizer.vercel.app/): interactive demos in the browser.
- Timothy B. Lee and Sean Trott, [*"Large language models, explained with a minimum of math and jargon"*](https://www.understandingai.org/p/large-language-models-explained-with).
- Messeri & Crockett (2024), [*"Artificial intelligence and illusions of understanding in scientific research"*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07146-0), *Nature*.

## Git, GitHub, and the web

- [GitHub Desktop docs](https://docs.github.com/en/desktop)
- [GitHub Pages docs](https://docs.github.com/en/pages)
- [Quarto websites](https://quarto.org/docs/websites/)

## Agents and skills

- [Claude Code docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview)
- Anthropic, [*"Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills"*](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/equipping-agents-for-the-real-world-with-agent-skills)
- [markitdown](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown): convert documents to Markdown so an agent can read them with fewer tokens.

## Tools for building things

- Images: the [Gemini API image generation docs](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/image-generation) (Nano Banana) and [Pillow](https://pillow.readthedocs.io/) for editing images with Python.
- Animation: [Manim](https://www.manim.community/) and [matplotlib animations](https://matplotlib.org/stable/api/animation_api.html).
- Sound and music: [music21](https://www.music21.org/music21docs/) and [pydub](https://github.com/jiaaro/pydub).
- HTML to PDF: [Playwright for Python](https://playwright.dev/python/) and [WeasyPrint](https://weasyprint.org/).
- Data visualization: [polars](https://pola.rs/), [plotnine](https://plotnine.org/), and [holtzy/dataviz-skills](https://github.com/holtzy/dataviz-skills).
- Slides: [Quarto presentations](https://quarto.org/docs/presentations/).

## AI and education

- The [MIT report on AI and education](https://aiandeducation.mit.edu/report/).
- Advait Sarkar, [*"How to stop AI from killing your critical thinking"*](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3lPnN8omdPA) (TED).
